_comment: ALLOWED DEVIATIONS — places where the implementation deliberately does NOT match the
Figma Design 2.0 frames. Without this file a 'drive the diff to zero' harness would push
us to ship accessibility failures, because several Design 2.0 pairings fail WCAG AA as
drawn (white on the GO LIVE green is 1.91:1).
EVERY ENTRY IS A GATE, NOT A COMMENT. Each carries a `requires` bound and a `measured`
value, and scripts/vp_compare.py RE-MEASURES from the capture on every run. An entry whose
region no longer meets its bound goes RED. That is the whole point: an entry that cannot
fail would authorise the drift it exists to prevent — the next reviewer reads
'intentional' and moves on.
FIELDS
capture/regions   which captured surface + which declared region (see surfaces.json)
metric            contrast | effective_opacity | text_matches
requires          the bound + WHICH WCAG threshold applies and why. PRD NFR-020 sets
4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text AND non-text UI, so an
entry that does not name its threshold cannot be checked correctly.
(large text = >=24px, or >=18.66px at weight >=700)
figma             what the source frame draws, and what it measures — the known-bad
value, which doubles as the mutation target when proving the entry
can fail.
measured          the value recorded when the entry was written, with its method.
vp_compare re-measures and reports drift against it.
category          source-defect (the Figma frame is wrong) |
semantic-divergence (our behaviour differs, so our visual must too)
permanence        permanent | retires-on-source-fix   — plus `retire_when` in prose.
Without this someone will reasonably try to clear the whole list
after a Figma correction, including the entries that must survive it.
Contrast is computed COMPOSITED — ink over every candidate backdrop (all gradient stops)
at the product of every ancestor's opacity. Token-pair maths alone certified the disabled
screens card as passing while a human saw 1.86:1, because the 0.5 lived on the card, not
the control.

deviations.retire_when: Never. The shipped ink IS the audited AA value; a corrected Figma frame should adopt it rather than the reverse.

figma.draws: white label on the broadcast-green gradient #3ed39a -> #28a579
figma.verdict: fails AA-normal (4.5) AND AA-large (3.0) at the light stop

implementation.ships: dark ink #06231a on the same green gradient

requires.why: the GO LIVE label renders at 14px weight 600 — below the 18.66px-bold large-text floor, so 3:1 does not apply

deviations.reason: GO LIVE is the primary broadcast control; its label must be readable across the whole gradient, not only at the dark end.

deviations.retire_when: Never. #a3283a is the canonical white-on-fill red; --sc-live is an INK token, correct for glyphs on dark, wrong as a fill under white text.

figma.verdict: fails AA-normal; clears AA-large, but this label is 14px/600, so AA-large does not apply

implementation.ships: white on the canonical white-on-fill red #a3283a -> #8f2030

requires.why: 14px weight 600 label; and BLACKOUT is safety-critical — it must stay readable in both idle and engaged states

deviations.reason: Emergency control. A 3.27:1 label on the one button an operator reaches for under pressure is not an acceptable fidelity trade.

deviations.retire_when: Never, unless --sc-primary-hover itself is darkened in the source. The constraint is already pinned as AA-large in selahcue-present/tests/test_tokens.rs (`design2_palette_meets_wcag_aa`).

figma.draws: white on the primary gradient topping out at --sc-primary-hover #7e6eff
figma.verdict: AA-large only — legitimate for large type, NOT for these 13-14px labels

requires.why: topbar GO LIVE is 13px/600 and Start is 14px/700 — both below the 18.66px-bold large-text floor

deviations.reason: The violet gradient is fine behind large type; these two buttons carry small labels, so the fill has to be the darker one.

deviations.retire_when: Never. This follows from OUR semantics, not from a Figma error: a closed card is the only route back to an open output window, so its meta line carries 'No output window' and must be readable. It stays stepped up even if the muted token is corrected.

figma.verdict: AA-large only — correct for supplementary micro-text, wrong for a line that now carries recovery-critical status

requires.why: 12px weight 500 status text, not a decorative caption

deviations.reason: Window semantics made this line load-bearing: it reports whether an OS output window exists.

deviations.retire_when: Never. Dimming the whole card is what dropped these controls to 1.8-2.8:1; the narrowing to .scr-thumb is the fix.

figma.draws: a disabled screen card dimmed as a whole
figma.verdict: the composited result fails AA badly on precisely the controls needed to re-open the window

implementation.ships: opacity 0.5 scoped to `.scr-card.screen-disabled .scr-thumb` only; controls stay at 1.0

requires.why: the CONTROLS on a closed card must not be dimmed at all; the thumbnail carries the 'no picture' signal instead

measured.method: product of every ancestor's computed opacity, element to root

deviations.reason: A closed card is the only route back to an open output window. Reading opacity on the control alone is a tautology here — the old rule put 0.5 on the CARD.

deviations.retire_when: Never — this is the positive control for the entry above.

implementation.ships: the preview thumbnail — and only it — at opacity 0.5

requires.why: POSITIVE CONTROL. Without it, 'the controls are not dimmed' would also pass if the dimming mechanism were deleted entirely — a dead mechanism and a correctly-scoped one would be indistinguishable.

measured.method: product of every ancestor's computed opacity, element to root

deviations.reason: The thumbnail is the thing that would have shown a picture, so 'nothing is being output' belongs there.

deviations.retire_when: Never. Window language is correct for a built-in screen (its OS window really is closed) and must never leak onto a virtual feed, which has no window.

figma.draws: a disabled screen pill reading MUTED
figma.verdict: wrong for built-in main/stage screens under window semantics

implementation.ships: CLOSED on a disabled BUILT-IN screen; MUTED stays for virtual feeds

requires.why: toggling a built-in screen off destroys its OS output window; calling that MUTED misdescribes what happened and what the toggle will do

measured.method: rendered textContent of the pill in the captured state

deviations.reason: Behavioural divergence with a visual consequence; the behaviour itself is gated by scripts/operator_headless.py.
